reading.body:
A point tagged as a data center in Siena, Italy is an accounting firm, not compute infrastructure. The name E. D. Accounting Siena identifies a bookkeeping practice, and the tag most plausibly reflects its own small server room or network closet.

The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no website. That combination is what a misapplied tag looks like rather than a facility that was surveyed and found small. An accounting office runs office computing and may hold client financial records on a local server, which is a different function from commercial colocation or cloud hosting.

For AI scaling this entry is a negative result. It adds no capacity to any count of Italian data centers and should not be read as one. The useful signal is about the underlying map: a tag that reads telecom=data_center can land on an ordinary business, so any tally built from that tag needs name-level review before it is treated as a building with power and compute inside.

What the data does not cover is how many other points carry the same error, or whether any real facility stands at these coordinates. It records one determination for one point, sourced to a tagging review, and nothing about the grid, land, or power that would make a site buildable.
